history.heading: Korean kingdoms
paragraphs: According to legend, the first Korean kingdom, Gojoseon, was founded in 2333 BCE. During the Three Kingdoms period, Goguryeo, Baekje and Silla competed for the peninsula until Silla unified most of it in 668. Silla's capital, Gyeongju, is rich in Buddhist monuments.

The Goryeo dynasty (918–1392), which gave Korea its name, produced celadon pottery and the world's oldest surviving book printed with movable metal type (1377). The Joseon dynasty (1392–1910) adopted Confucianism; King Sejong the Great created the Hangul alphabet in 1443.

history.heading: Colonial rule and division
paragraphs: Japan annexed Korea in 1910 and ruled it harshly, suppressing Korean culture and mobilising labour, including "comfort women" forced into sexual slavery. The March 1st Movement of 1919 was a major independence protest.

After Japan's defeat in 1945, the peninsula was divided, with the US occupying the south. The Republic of Korea was founded in 1948 under Syngman Rhee. North Korea invaded in 1950, and the Korean War (1950–53) devastated the country before ending in an armistice.

history.heading: Miracle on the Han River
paragraphs: Under General Park Chung-hee, who seized power in 1961, South Korea industrialised at extraordinary speed, transforming from one of the poorest countries into a wealthy economy. Authoritarian rule continued, and the 1980 Gwangju Uprising was brutally suppressed. Mass protests in 1987 brought democracy.

South Korea hosted the 1988 Olympics and recovered from the 1997 Asian financial crisis. President Park Geun-hye was impeached in 2017. In December 2024, President Yoon Suk Yeol declared martial law for a few hours; he was impeached and removed, and Lee Jae-myung won the June 2025 presidential election.

culture.heading: Hallyu
paragraphs: Korean is the official language, written in Hangul. Many South Koreans are non-religious, with significant Protestant, Buddhist and Catholic populations. Confucian values of family, education and respect for elders remain strong.

The "Korean Wave" (Hallyu) has made K-pop (BTS, Blackpink), K-dramas and films such as Parasite, which won the Oscar for Best Picture, globally popular. Han Kang won the Nobel Prize in Literature in 2024.

culture.heading: Food and traditions
paragraphs: Korean cuisine features kimchi (recognised by UNESCO), bibimbap, bulgogi, Korean barbecue and tteokbokki. Seollal (Lunar New Year) and Chuseok (harvest festival) are major holidays. Taekwondo originated in Korea; baseball, football and esports are hugely popular.

politics.heading: Presidential republic
paragraphs: South Korea is a presidential republic. The president serves a single five-year term, and the National Assembly is unicameral. Politics is highly polarised between conservatives and progressives.

The alliance with the United States, which stations around 28,000 troops in Korea, is central to security against North Korea. Relations with Japan have improved but remain sensitive over history. China is the largest trading partner.

economy.heading: A technology powerhouse
paragraphs: South Korea has one of the world's largest economies. Conglomerates (chaebol) such as Samsung, Hyundai, SK and LG lead in semiconductors (Samsung and SK Hynix are among the largest memory chip makers), smartphones, cars, shipbuilding, batteries and steel. It has some of the world's fastest internet.

The currency is the won. South Korea has the world's lowest fertility rate, under one child per woman, creating major demographic challenges, along with high household debt, housing costs and intense educational competition.
